FreeBSD on the desktop? Am I crazy? [xpost /v/BSD]

I've been using it on my laptop for about a week. Installing with full disk encryption using ZFS and Geli and painless, but the post-install experience has not been without its challenges. I need to run CURRENT in order for my wireless card to be supported and have proper Ivy Bridge graphics support, but I don't mind contributing bug reports and working around problems here and there. KDE 4 works well. Pkg is a breeze to use coming from the Linux world. The only major hiccup was transferring my backed files over from a ext4-formatted external hard drive became an exercise in virtualizing Debian using bhyve in order to mount the the drive and then rsyncing the files over. Mounting the drive with Fuse wasn't working for some reason. But hey, at least I learned something. I've even got the system automatically mounting a samba share I set up on my network so transferring files around will be easier in the future. Getting good looking fonts has been a little annoying. I've had to do a lot of wrangling with /usr/local/etc/fonts/local.conf and some of the prefab settings in conf.d to get autohinting, antialiasing and to override to certain better fonts than the terrible-looking Helvetica and Times New Roman fonts. I really like the way things are set up with a stable base system, rolling release ports, and an otherwise sane development process. My desktop experience has been overall very nice, and I've got everything I need to get work done. Once 11 ships I expect I will settle down to running STABLE. Until then, I'm enjoying lurking the mailing lists and getting to know this excellent community.

I have started using GhostBSD on a spare computer, and in many ways, it is up to speed with an "out of the box" Linux experience. Multimedia codecs, quick installation of new browsers through the command line or Octopkg, and the same productivity and text editing software that can sustain me 90% of the time. Things sure have come a long way since I ran NetBSD off a live disc on a Sega Dreamcast. :-)
To be fair, GhostBSD is a preconfigured FreeBSD, NetBSD is still an acquired taste. :)
